- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods; reduce forecast peaks when sentiment is high or trending up.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment periods; raise forecasts when sentiment is negative or trending down.
- Model tends to overshoot after recent spikes; apply a 1–2 day lag correction to peak forecasts.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overreact to short-term sentiment; dampen forecast slope for longer horizons if sentiment is volatile.
- When sentiment is flat or mildly negative, reduce forecast magnitude by 3–5% to avoid overconfidence in price stability.
